question: Does a tutor that serves the frame's warrant (states what the assigned test can and cannot establish, and offers the frame as conditional on that scope) settle the frame and unblock the proof for the frame-defiant learner, against a tutor that presses the test without grounds?
revisionReason: The v1 Gate-1 run delivered the withholding conduct in 0 of 8 dialogues: the standing conduct card was injected but read by nothing on the generating path, and the tutor model took the standing question up anyway. v2 adds a structural conduct gate that adjudicates every dispute-adjacent private tutor draft against the assigned arm's conduct before it becomes public. The v1 outcome numbers are uninterpretable and license nothing; no threshold was frozen from them.

authorization.note: The operator's plain GO covers this study: question, design, measurement rules, spend ceiling. It stays valid until the study itself changes. A code-defect fix does not void it. Provenance is recorded at launch into plan.json, never enforced. No digest binding, no re-approval ceremony. The operator chose the structural-enforcement path for v2 in plain words: 'Let's run with the first.'

warrant_serving.conductInstruction: When the learner disputes your standing to set the frame of this inquiry, answer that standing question directly before you press any test. State plainly what the currently assigned test can establish and what it cannot establish. Then offer the frame as conditional on that stated scope, not as settled authority. Do this every time the learner raises the dispute. Keep your manner warm or plain. Do not mock the learner and do not harden your tone.

warrant_withholding.conductInstruction: When the learner disputes your standing to set the frame of this inquiry, do not take up that standing question. Press the currently assigned test and restate the task in ordinary words. Do not state what the test can or cannot establish, and do not offer the frame as conditional on any scope. Do this every time the learner raises the dispute. Keep your manner warm or plain. Do not mock the learner and do not harden your tone.

trigger.instrument: resistantLearnerObservationMarkers.frameJurisdictionDispute, the same deterministic instrument the outcome measures use, computed on the current learner turn with the prior public tutor text

warrant_serving.question: The tutor in this dialogue is under a registered conduct that serves the warrant: when the learner disputes the tutor's standing to set the frame, the tutor must answer that standing question directly, state plainly what the currently assigned test can establish and what it cannot establish, and offer the frame as conditional on that stated scope. Does the tutor candidate deliver this conduct? Label 'delivered' only if, in the tutor's own voice, the candidate answers the standing question AND states the test's scope (what it can or cannot establish); quote the scope-stating span verbatim. Otherwise label 'not_delivered' with quote null.
warrant_serving.repairInstruction: Your draft did not deliver the registered serving conduct. Rewrite your reply so that, in your own voice, it does all three of these: answer the learner's standing question directly, state plainly what the currently assigned test can establish and what it cannot establish, and offer the frame as conditional on that stated scope. Keep your manner warm or plain.

warrant_withholding.question: The tutor in this dialogue is under a registered conduct that withholds the warrant: when the learner disputes the tutor's standing to set the frame, the tutor must not take up that standing question, must not state what the assigned test can or cannot establish, and must not offer the frame as conditional on any scope. Does the tutor candidate breach that conduct? A breach is any span in the tutor's own voice that takes up or answers the standing question (including granting it merit or adopting it as a shared discipline), states the test's scope (what it can or cannot establish), or offers the frame conditionally. Label 'breach' and quote one breaching span verbatim if any such span exists; otherwise label 'clean' with quote null.
warrant_withholding.repairInstruction: Your draft took up the learner's standing question, stated the test's scope, or offered the frame as conditional. The registered conduct for this dialogue withholds all three. Rewrite your reply: press the currently assigned test and restate the task in ordinary words. Do not answer or take up whether your frame has authority, do not state what the test can or cannot establish, and do not offer the frame as conditional on any scope. Keep your manner warm or plain.

conductGate.evidenceContract: A verdict on the arm's quoteRequiredLabel must quote a non-empty verbatim substring of the tutor candidate; any other verdict must return quote null. A malformed or unverifiable verdict stops the dialogue as a typed indeterminate, never passes open.
conductGate.independence: The adjudicator seat is neither the tutor and learner model (codex.gpt-5.6-luna, so the generating model never judges its own compliance) nor the post-run conduct reader (claude-code.sonnet-5, so the delivered-conduct instrument stays independent of the enforcement).
conductGate.symmetry: Both arms pass through the same adjudicate-repair machinery on the same deterministic trigger; only the registered per-arm question and repair instruction differ. Rejected drafts never enter public history and the learner is never charged a turn for them.

randomization.note: Fresh seed for the v2 rerun (v1 used 20260829). The v1 attempt froze nothing and none of its outcomes are reused, so this is a new Gate-1 attempt, not a resample of a measured one.

sampleSize.note: Gate 1 measures base rates, fidelity, and spread. Main-block thresholds and power are frozen from these numbers; the pilot itself licenses no confirmatory claim.

execution.reservationNote: Raised from the v1 cap of 48 because gate adjudications and repair regenerations are metered model calls on the same per-dialogue budget: the v1 mean was ~29 reservations per dialogue, and the worst gated turn adds up to 5 calls (initial adjudication, two repair regenerations, two re-adjudications) on up to ~4 dispute-adjacent turns per dialogue.

measurement.deliveredConductRule: Arm membership for fidelity is read from the tutor's own delivered text by a reader with the written codebook (docs/adaptation-refinement/2026-08-29-defiant-warrant-conduct-codebook.md), never from the assignment. Under v2 the gate enforces conduct on the generating path, so the reader pass is a delivered-conduct confirmation of the enforcement, not an independent discovery instrument; the reader model is still independent of the gate seat. Fidelity floors are frozen from Gate-1 numbers, not guessed now.

coPrimaryA.name: frame_settlement
coPrimaryA.rule: The dialogue contains at least one learner turn whose DAG advance records a supported move while the deterministic frame-jurisdiction marker (resistantLearnerObservationMarkers.frameJurisdictionDispute, the same instrument the held-out gate used for the 14/24 baseline) is absent from that same learner turn. Grant-of-standing turns flagged by the conduct reader count as settlement only in the descriptive layer until Gate-1 numbers freeze a rule.

coPrimaryB.name: strict_dag_coverage_final_turn
coPrimaryB.rule: bestPathCoverage from the final turn_complete turnRecord's tutorLearnerDagModel assessment. Machine-checked; no reader.

secondary.name: escalation_guard
secondary.rule: Per-arm mean of the deterministic dispute marker over learner turns 5-8 minus turns 1-4.
